main_text.l: orum super fortem iustorum: ne exten-dant iusti ad iniquitatem manus suas. Est.13.17: Sorti tuæ esto propitius.

5. Possessionem communem bonorū seu spiritualium, seu corporaliū. De spiritualium bonorū possessione dicitur: Gratias agentes Patri, qui idoneos nos fecit ad participandam sortem Sanctorum in luce. Col.1.12. De privatione autem horum bonorum dicitur: Non est tibi pars neque sors in hoc negotio. Act.8.21.

6. Officium. De Iuda Iscariota dicitur Act.1.17. Quia annumerabatur nobiscū, & sortitus erat partem (κλήρου[?]) ministerij huius, &c. Daniel.12. Tu autem stabis in sorte tua. De hoc dicto, an ne de officio accipi debeat, iudiciū alijs permitto.

Sortes hoc loco significat ceremonias varias, in quibus, adhibitis ex pacto certis quibusdam testeris, Deo indicium iudiciumq; de personis aut reb. permittitur, ut finis sit suspicionum & controuersiarum. Hæc finitio per causarum & fortiū praxeos ἀντιγραφὴν[?] sic illustrabitur.
Proverb.16.33. In sinum proijcitur sors, sed a Iehoua est omne iudicium eius. παρὰ κυρίου[?], & gubernator euentus in forti-tio-

page.notes: Greek words in the text are doubtful: "κλήρου" (printed in a worn form), "ἀντιγραφὴν" (the word after praxeos is badly printed) and "παρὰ κυρίου" (the opening letters are unclear). All three are marked [?]. The "7" of the page number is worn but reads 78. The lower-right "tio-" is a catchword, and the text ends with "in forti-". The text also has the long-s forms "s" and ligature "Æ" in the running head, which are normalised here. A stray "/" mark at the foot is not printed text and is left out.
